name: Spec: Gmail account contract — model fields, OAuth scopes, API surface
description:
PREREQUISITE for the Gmail milestones. Backend and front-end must agree on one contract before coding starts, otherwise the two workstreams diverge.

Profile chosen: analyst — this task is about writing precise, testable requirements, not code.

DELIVERABLE: a written spec (docs) defining:
1. GmailAccount model fields to add to CodxUser (api/codx/junior/model/user.py): id, email address, display name, granted scopes, token expiry, status (connected/expired/revoked/error), created_at, last_error. Explicitly define where the refresh token is stored and that it must NEVER be returned by any API response.
2. Required Google OAuth scopes per milestone: M1 connect (openid, email, profile), M2 read (gmail.readonly), M3 send (gmail.send). Note that gmail.send is needed to send, gmail.readonly for reading, and that adding a scope later forces re-consent.
3. Exact REST API surface (paths, verbs, request/response JSON) for: list accounts, start connect (auth url), OAuth callback, disconnect/revoke, list messages, get message, send message.
4. Error/edge cases: expired refresh token, revoked access, quota exceeded, account already connected.
5. Acceptance criteria per milestone, written so a demo can verify them.

CONSTRAINTS: follow existing project conventions — CodxUser is a pydantic model persisted through global_settings sections; OAuth precedent is api/codx/junior/security/github_oauth.py; OAuth provider config comes from get_oauth_provider() with env convention CODX_{PROVIDER}_CLIENT_ID / _SECRET / _TOKEN_URL.

ACCEPTANCE: spec committed under docs/, and it is specific enough that backend and front-end can be built in parallel without further negotiation.
